anomaly_def.Name: Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standbys or downstream consumers cannot receive, persist, or apply primary-generated log records at the pace they are produced, causing growing log-position gaps and replay lag.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk data or index pages are physically or logically corrupted so that stored structures no longer match the expected logical contents, yielding wrong or incomplete query results and engine corruption errors.

When both root causes are present, the database estate exhibits a compound failure surface: replicas fall behind while simultaneously applying corrupt or inconsistent pages, leading to divergent data sets. Symptoms include replay lag that never clears, replica crashes or endless retries on specific LSNs, replication pipelines stalling on checksum or key-order errors, primary log segments retained indefinitely, unexpected duplicate or missing rows on replicas, inconsistent read results between primary and replicas, and integrity-check utilities flagging escalating corruption footprints on both sides. Failover readiness is severely degraded because the most current replica is both out-of-date and structurally unreliable, and monitoring tools may misattribute performance degradation to network or I/O saturation while underlying corruption silently spreads.

Causally, sustained replication lag lengthens the window during which damaged pages created on the primary (or introduced by storage faults on a replica) propagate. Conversely, corrupted pages encountered during apply can throttle or halt the single-threaded replay worker, amplifying lag and causing the primary to retain more WAL, which increases I/O pressure and the chance of further corruption on an already stressed storage subsystem. The feedback loop—corruption causing replay stalls, and stalls increasing exposure of corrupted state—accelerates divergence and magnifies both anomalies, ultimately threatening data consistency, availability, and recoverability across the cluster.

entry.official_definition: Read timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol read operation exceeds mysqlx_read_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network read operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
